title: Interacting particle mean field and vortex blob error

items.title: Bounded-Lipschitz dual discrepancy for finite signed measures
items.statement:
Let $\omega,
u$ be finite signed Borel measures on $\mathbb R^d$ such that $|\omega-
u|(\mathbb R^d)<\infty$. For each bounded Lipschitz test function, integration against $\omega-
u$ is defined by [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]; boundedness and finite total variation make every test in the following set integrable. Set $\|\phi\|_\infty:=\sup_x|\phi(x)|$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\phi):=\sup_{x
e y}|\phi(x)-\phi(y)|/|x-y|$, with $\operatorname{Lip}(\phi)=0$ when $d=0$, using the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Define the bounded-Lipschitz dual discrepancy
$$d_{BL}(\omega,
u):=\sup\left\{\left|\int\phi\,d(\omega-
u)ight|:\|\phi\|_\infty\le1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(\phi)\le1ight\}.$$
The integral bound by total variation shows this supremum is finite. This page uses only the displayed dual quantity and makes no separate metric-separation claim. No Jordan decomposition, positivity, or probability normalization is needed.
items.axiom_use: The bounded-Lipschitz dual discrepancy is choice-free; the integral is the published signed-measure integral on its L1 domain.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Globally Lipschitz mean-field interaction kernel
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, with the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. An interaction kernel is a continuous map $K:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$. It is globally Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ in the convention used on this page if
$$|K(x,y)-K(x',y')|\le L(|x-x'|+|y-y'|)$$
for all $x,y,x',y'\in\mathbb R^d$. This implies the linear-growth estimate
$$|K(x,y)|\le |K(0,0)|+L(|x|+|y|).$$
The notation $L$ always refers to this two-variable convention; the stability factor below is therefore $2L$.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
Simon Mayer, The Vlasov Equation and Mean Field Limit of a Particle System

items.title: Smooth mollified Biot-Savart kernel
items.statement:
In two dimensions let $z^\perp=(-z_2,z_1)$ and
$$G(z)=\frac1{2\pi}\log|z|,\qquad K(z)=\nabla^\perp G(z)=\frac{z^\perp}{2\pi|z|^2}\quad(z\ne0).$$
The locally integrable value assigned to $K(0)$ is immaterial. Fix a radial, nonnegative smooth bump $\rho$ supported in the unit ball with $\int\rho=1$; its scaled family is the mollifier family of [[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]. Put $\rho_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-2}\rho(z/\varepsilon)$, $G_\varepsilon=G*\rho_\varepsilon$, and
$$K_\varepsilon=K*\rho_\varepsilon.$$
The kernel is a regularized interaction; its smoothness and global Lipschitz property are proved in a separate lemma. It does not define the singular physical interaction at a collision.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition.

references.title: J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data
Gregory R. Baker and Lan D. Pham, A Comparison of Blob Methods for Vortex Sheet Roll Up

items.title: The coupling definition of the 1-Wasserstein distance
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. For Borel probability measures $\mu,
u$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moments $\int |x|\,d\mu(x)<\infty$ and $\int |y|\,d
u(y)<\infty$, let $\Pi(\mu,
u)$ be the set of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d	imes\mathbb R^d$ whose first and second marginals are $\mu$ and $
u$. Define
$$W_1(\mu,
u):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,
u)}\int_{\mathbb R^d	imes\mathbb R^d}|x-y|\,d\pi(x,y).$$
This definition makes no assertion that the infimum is attained. It applies only to probability measures with finite first moment; it is not a distance assigned here to a general signed measure.

Here $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and probability measure has the meaning of [[def-probability-measure]].
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Sign-preserving transport cost for finite signed measures
items.statement:
Assume $d\ge1$ and the Axiom of Choice when invoking [[thm-jordan-decomposition-for-signed-measures]]. Let $\omega,
u$ be finite signed Borel measures on $\mathbb R^d$ whose total variations have finite first moments, and use the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Write their Jordan parts as $\omega^+,\omega^-$ and $
u^+,
u^-$. If the positive-part masses agree and the negative-part masses agree, define using finite nonnegative Borel measures $\pi^\pm$ on $\mathbb R^d	imes\mathbb R^d$ whose first and second marginals are respectively the corresponding positive or negative Jordan parts:
$$C_{\pm}(\omega,
u):=\inf_{\pi^+,\pi^-}\left(\int|x-y|d\pi^+(x,y)+\int|x-y|d\pi^-(x,y)ight),$$
where $\pi^+$ ranges over finite nonnegative couplings of $\omega^+$ and $
u^+$, and $\pi^-$ over finite nonnegative couplings of $\omega^-$ and $
u^-$. The infimum is over both sign couplings independently. This cost is not the probability $W_1$.
items.axiom_use: The canonical Jordan parts used here are supplied by a theorem whose general existence branch assumes the Axiom of Choice.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data

items.title: Completeness of the weighted continuous trajectory space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(E,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a probability space, $T>0$, and $d\ge1$. Use the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Let $\mathcal X$ be the space, modulo equality $\mu$-almost everywhere, of jointly measurable maps $X:[0,T]\times E\to\mathbb R^d$ whose paths are continuous for almost every label and whose time-supremum function is measurable, and for which
$$\|X\|_{\mathcal X}:=\int_E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t(z)|d\mu(z)<\infty.$$
In this formula and in $\|X-Y\|_{\mathcal X}$, take the supremum on a measurable conull set where the relevant paths are continuous and extend it by zero off that set; equality almost everywhere means equality of whole paths outside one measurable null set. The seminorm identifies maps equal almost everywhere, and the induced distance $d_{\mathcal X}(X,Y)=\|X-Y\|_{\mathcal X}$ is a metric on the quotient; it is complete.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice selects measurable representatives of the countable sequence of equivalence classes; least-index subsequence selection is choice-free.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Tensor composite Simpson force evaluator on a rectangle
items.statement: Input real endpoints $a,b,c,d$, integer panel counts $n_x,n_y$, and an exact evaluation oracle that, when queried at a point, returns either a value in $\mathbb R^2$ or evaluation-failure. First, if $a\ge b$ or $c\ge d$, return invalid-domain without querying the oracle. Next, if either panel count is odd or is less than two, return invalid-panel-count without querying the oracle. For the remaining inputs set $R=[a,b]\times[c,d]$, $h_x=(b-a)/n_x$, $h_y=(d-c)/n_y$, $x_i=a+ih_x$ for $0\le i\le n_x$, and $y_j=c+jh_y$ for $0\le j\le n_y$. Query the oracle at every grid point in lexicographic order with $i$ first and $j$ second, storing the returned values. If a query fails, stop at the first such point and return evaluation-failure with that point. Otherwise, for each $j$ form the continuous piecewise-linear interpolant through the stored values $F(x_i,y_j)$ and apply [[alg-composite-simpson-rule]] componentwise in $x$ to this interpolant, obtaining $G_j=Q_xF(\cdot,y_j)$. Form the continuous piecewise-linear interpolant through the stored $G_j$ and apply the same valid Simpson procedure componentwise in $y$ to obtain $Q_yG=Q_yQ_xF$. Return this vector $Q_yQ_xF$. Each interpolant is queried only at its stored grid nodes, so no new oracle call is needed. Both calls to the supplier use strictly ordered endpoints and even panel counts at least two. This is an exact-real procedure; termination and force-accuracy bounds are established in [[thm-tensor-simpson-force-error]], and floating-point roundoff is outside its scope.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; the procedure is a finite exact-arithmetic sum.

references.title: Tobin Driscoll and Richard Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, Section 5.6
MIT OpenCourseWare 18.330, Introduction to Numerical Analysis, Chapter 5

items.title: Characteristic solution of a probability mean-field equation
items.statement:
Fix $T>0$, a globally Lipschitz kernel $K$ as in [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]], and a Borel probability measure $\mu_0$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moment as in [[def-p-one-wasserstein-one]]. A characteristic solution on $[0,T]$ consists of a jointly Borel map $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$, defined up to a $\mu_0$-null set of labels, such that $t\mapsto X_t(x)$ is absolutely continuous for $\mu_0$-almost every $x$, $X_0(x)=x$, and
$$X_t(x)=x+\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(X_s(x),X_s(y))\,d\mu_0(y)\,ds$$
for $\mu_0$-almost every $x$. It transports $\mu_0$ to $\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0$, where $(X_t)_\#\mu_0(A):=\mu_0(X_t^{-1}(A))$. The weighted path integrability convention is $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t(x)|d\mu_0(x)<\infty$; in particular every time slice has finite first moment.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Equal-probability mean-field and weighted signed vortex particle systems
items.statement:
For a globally Lipschitz interaction kernel $K$ and $N\ge1$, the equal-probability mean-field particle system is
$$\dot x_i(t)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N K(x_i(t),x_j(t)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N.$$
Its empirical probability measure is $\mu_N(t)=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$.

For a mollified two-dimensional Biot-Savart kernel $K_\varepsilon$ from [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]] and real weights $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_N$, the weighted signed vortex particle system is
$$\dot x_i(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i(t)-x_j(t)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,$$
with vorticity measure $\omega_N(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$. If $\Gamma_i=1/N$ and $K(x,y)=K_\varepsilon(x-y)$, the first system is the probability special case. The weighted signed system is a first-order Biot-Savart model.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in these finite systems.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data

items.title: Characteristic solution for a finite signed regularized vorticity
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $\omega_0$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb R^2$, set $M=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2)$, and let $\omega_0=\omega_0^+-\omega_0^-$ be its Jordan decomposition. The Jordan total-variation formula gives $M=\omega_0^+(\mathbb R^2)+\omega_0^-(\mathbb R^2)$. If $M=0$, its characteristic solution is the constant zero measure curve. If $M>0$, set $E=\mathbb R^2\times\{+1,-1\}$ with sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^2)\otimes 2^{\{+1,-1\}}$, and define the probability measure $\lambda_0$ by $\lambda_0(A\times\{s\})=\omega_0^s(A)/M$ for Borel $A$ and $s\in\{+1,-1\}$; its total mass is one by the displayed formula. A signed characteristic solution for the regularized kernel $K_\varepsilon$ on $[0,T]$ is a jointly measurable path map $Z:[0,T]\times E\to\mathbb R^2$, modulo $\lambda_0$-almost everywhere equality, with absolutely continuous paths for almost every label, $Z_0(x,s)=x$, and

$$Z_t(x,s)=x+M\int_0^t\int_E rK_\varepsilon(Z_u(x,s)-Z_u(y,r))\,d\lambda_0(y,r)\,du,$$

such that its time-supremum function is measurable and $\int_E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|Z_t(x,s)|\,d\lambda_0(x,s)<\infty$. It represents the signed measure curve

$$\omega_t=M\int_E s\,\delta_{Z_t(x,s)}\,d\lambda_0(x,s).$$

Here $\omega_0^s$ denotes $\omega_0^+$ when $s=+1$ and $\omega_0^-$ when $s=-1$. The total variation mass is $M$ at time zero, and the sign coordinate records each Jordan part separately.
items.axiom_use: The definition uses canonical Jordan parts, whose general existence supplier assumes AC.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data

items.title: The mollified Biot-Savart kernel is smooth and globally Lipschitz
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the mollifier of [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. For every $\varepsilon>0$, $G_\varepsilon$ and $K_\varepsilon$ are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^2$, and there is $C_\rho<\infty$ independent of $\varepsilon$ such that
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}\|DK_\varepsilon(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_\rho\varepsilon^{-2}.$$
Consequently $K_\varepsilon$ is globally Lipschitz with constant at most $C_\rho\varepsilon^{-2}$.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is required by the smooth-convolution and polar-coordinate suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

references.title: J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data
Gregory R. Baker and Lan D. Pham, A Comparison of Blob Methods for Vortex Sheet Roll Up

items.title: The bounded-Lipschitz dual discrepancy is bounded by split transport cost
items.statement:
Assume AC for the Jordan decompositions in [[def-signed-split-transport-cost]]. Let $d\ge1$. If finite signed Borel measures $\omega,
u$ on $\mathbb R^d$ have the same positive-part mass and the same negative-part mass, and their total variations have finite first moments, then the couplings in $C_{\pm}(\omega,
u)$ exist, $C_{\pm}(\omega,
u)<\infty$, and
$$d_{BL}(\omega,
u)\le C_{\pm}(\omega,
u).$$
items.axiom_use: The Jordan parts use the Axiom of Choice; the coupling inequality after the parts are supplied is choice-free.

references.title: J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data
François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: The coupling infimum is finite for finite-first-moment probabilities
items.statement:
If $\mu,
u$ are Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moments, then $\Pi(\mu,
u)$ is nonempty and $W_1(\mu,
u)<\infty$ for the definition in [[def-p-one-wasserstein-one]].
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Separable regularized vortex-inspired Hamiltonian comparison system
items.statement:
For $N\ge2$, real weights $\Gamma_i$, and $\varepsilon>0$, define the open collision-free configuration set $Q_{cf}:=\{q=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in(\mathbb R^2)^N:q_i\ne q_j\text{ for }i\ne j\}$. Let $q\in Q_{cf}$ and $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_N)\in(\mathbb R^2)^N$. Let
$$H_\varepsilon(q,p)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^N|p_i|^2+V_\varepsilon(q),\qquad V_\varepsilon(q)=\sum_{i<j}\Gamma_i\Gamma_jG_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j),$$
where $G_\varepsilon$ is from [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. This is a separable canonical Hamiltonian on $Q_{cf}$; its local leapfrog map is the partial composition [[def-leapfrog-step-map]] restricted as in [[def-local-leapfrog-domain-on-an-open-configuration-set]]. It is a distinct second-order canonical comparison model, not the first-order Biot-Savart vortex system of [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]].
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition.

references.title: Ernst Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration, TU München Lecture 2: Symplectic integrators
Nikolaj Nordkvist and Poul G. Hjorth, Classical Mechanics and Symplectic Integration
J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data

items.title: Dobrushin stability in 1-Wasserstein distance for mean-field flows
items.statement:
Let $K$ have two-variable Lipschitz constant $L$ as in [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]], and let $\mu_t,
u_t$ be characteristic solutions from probability measures with finite first moments. For every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$W_1(\mu_t,
u_t)\le e^{2Lt}W_1(\mu_0,
u_0).$$
The estimate is proved for every prescribed initial coupling before taking the infimum; existence of an optimal coupling is not assumed.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; no optimal coupling is selected.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
Simon Mayer, The Vlasov Equation and Mean Field Limit of a Particle System

items.title: Exact weak mean-field identity for empirical particle measures
items.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_N$ solve the equal-probability system of [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]] on $[0,T]$, and put $\mu_N(t)=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$. Then for every $\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^d)$,
$$\int\varphi d\mu_N(t)-\int\varphi d\mu_N(0) =\int_0^t\int\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot\left(\int K(x,y)d\mu_N(s)(y)\right)d\mu_N(s)(x)ds.$$
Thus the empirical measure satisfies the same weak transport equation exactly, with no particle quadrature error in this identity.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; only a finite sum and the chain rule occur.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Global characteristic flow for a globally Lipschitz mean-field kernel
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be globally Lipschitz with constant $L$ in the convention of [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]], and let $\mu_0$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moment. For every finite $T>0$ there exists a characteristic solution on $[0,T]$ in the sense of [[def-characteristic-mean-field-solution]]. It is unique up to equality of trajectories for $\mu_0$-almost every label. No compact support assumption is needed.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice enters through weighted path-space completeness; the fixed-point iteration itself uses no further choice.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
Simon Mayer, The Vlasov Equation and Mean Field Limit of a Particle System

items.title: Weak transport identity for characteristic mean-field solutions
items.statement:
Let $\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0$ be the characteristic solution for a globally Lipschitz kernel on $[0,T]$. For every $\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^d)$ and $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\int\varphi\,d\mu_t-\int\varphi\,d\mu_0 =\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R^d}\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot\left(\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(x,y)d\mu_s(y)\right)d\mu_s(x)ds.$$
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this conditional weak-identity proof.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: L1 consistency of the mollified Biot-Savart kernel
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the radial compactly supported mollifier of [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. Write $\|F\|_{L^1}:=\int_{\mathbb R^2}|F(x)|dx$ and let $\|g\|_{L^\infty}$ be the essential supremum of $|g|$. There is a constant $C_\rho<\infty$, independent of $\varepsilon>0$, such that
$$\|K_\varepsilon-K\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_\rho\varepsilon.$$
Consequently, for every bounded measurable vorticity density $\omega$,
$$\|(K_\varepsilon-K)*\omega\|_{L^\infty}\le C_\rho\varepsilon\|\omega\|_{L^\infty}.$$
This is an error estimate at fixed $\varepsilon$; it does not prove a singular-limit theorem for the particle dynamics.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is required by the cited polar-coordinate measure formula; no full Axiom of Choice is used in this estimate.

references.title: J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data
Gregory R. Baker and Lan D. Pham, A Comparison of Blob Methods for Vortex Sheet Roll Up
François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Signed Dobrushin stability with bounded force defects
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $K_\varepsilon$ have one-variable Lipschitz constant $L_\varepsilon$; then $(x,y)\mapsto K_\varepsilon(x-y)$ has two-variable constant $L_\varepsilon$. Let $\omega_0,
u_0$ have separately matching positive and negative Jordan masses and total variation mass $M$. For $M>0$, use the Jordan-label probability spaces of [[def-signed-vorticity-characteristic-solution]] and suppose their path maps $X^\omega_t(x,s)$ and $X^
u_t(y,s)$ have integrable time suprema, satisfy $X^\omega_0(x,s)=x$ and $X^
u_0(y,s)=y$, and represent $\omega_t,
u_t$ by the signed pushforward formula there. Assume at each time the positive and negative label pushforwards are the Jordan parts. Write
$$u^\omega_t(x)=\int K_\varepsilon(x-z)d\omega_t(z),\qquad u^
u_t(y)=\int K_\varepsilon(y-z)d
u_t(z).$$
Suppose their absolutely continuous sign-labelled trajectories satisfy
$$\dot X^\omega_t(x,s)=u^\omega_t(X^\omega_t(x,s))+r_\omega(t,x,s),\qquad \dot X^
u_t(y,s)=u^
u_t(X^
u_t(y,s))+r_
u(t,y,s)$$
for almost every time and almost every label of sign $s\in\{+,-\}$, with $|r_\omega|\le\eta_\omega$ and $|r_
u|\le\eta_
u$ on $[0,T]$. For every prescribed initial pair of sign-preserving couplings of total cost $D_0$,
$$d_{BL}(\omega_t,
u_t)\le C_{\pm}(\omega_t,
u_t)\le e^{2L_\varepsilon Mt} igl(D_0+M(\eta_\omega+\eta_
u)t igr).$$
If $M=0$, both curves are zero and the inequalities hold with zero right side. Taking the infimum over initial couplings in the $M>0$ case gives the same bound with $D_0=C_{\pm}(\omega_0,
u_0)$, without assuming attainment.
items.axiom_use: AC supplies the Jordan parts. Countable Choice is used for the cited mollified-kernel regularity supplier; the stability estimate is conditional on the stated paths and uses no optimal split coupling.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
Simon Mayer, The Vlasov Equation and Mean Field Limit of a Particle System

items.title: Characteristic existence and total-variation preservation for regularized signed vorticity
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $\omega_0$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb R^2$ whose total variation has finite first moment, and let $K_\varepsilon$ be the smooth mollified Biot-Savart kernel of [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. There is a unique signed characteristic solution in the sense of [[def-signed-vorticity-characteristic-solution]] on every finite interval $[0,T]$, and it represents the measure curve with velocity
$$u_t(x)=\int K_\varepsilon(x-y)d\omega_t(y),\qquad \omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0.$$
The flow is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^2$ at each time and
$$|\omega_t|(\mathbb R^2)=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2).$$
If $\omega_0=0$, the only transported measure curve is identically zero.
items.axiom_use: The general Jordan decomposition invokes AC; weighted path-space completeness invokes Countable Choice. The local ODE and transport estimates add no choice principle.

references.title: J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data
Gregory R. Baker and Lan D. Pham, A Comparison of Blob Methods for Vortex Sheet Roll Up
François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Probability W1 stability under bounded force defects
items.statement:
Let $K$ have two-variable global Lipschitz constant $L$ as in [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]]. Let $\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0$ and $
u_t=(Y_t)_\#
u_0$ be probability curves from finite-first-moment initial laws, with absolutely continuous characteristic paths satisfying
$$\dot X_t(x)=\int K(X_t(x),X_t(z))d\mu_0(z)+r_\mu(t,x),\qquad \dot Y_t(y)=\int K(Y_t(y),Y_t(w))d
u_0(w)+r_
u(t,y)$$
for almost every time and almost every label, with $X_0(x)=x$ and $Y_0(y)=y$. Assume additionally the weighted path integrability conditions $\int\sup_{s\le T}|X_s|d\mu_0<\infty$ and $\int\sup_{s\le T}|Y_s|d
u_0<\infty$. Assume the measurable label defects satisfy $|r_\mu|\le\eta_\mu$ and $|r_
u|\le\eta_
u$ on $[0,T]$. For every prescribed initial coupling $\pi_0$ of cost $D_0$, its transport by the two characteristic paths has cost at time $t$ at most
$$e^{2Lt} igl(D_0+(\eta_\mu+\eta_
u)t igr).$$
Consequently $W_1(\mu_t,
u_t)\le e^{2Lt} igl(W_1(\mu_0,
u_0)+(\eta_\mu+\eta_
u)t igr)$. The estimate is first proved for each coupling; no optimal plan is assumed.
items.axiom_use: No choice is used in the coupling estimate; an optimal coupling is not assumed.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1
Simon Mayer, The Vlasov Equation and Mean Field Limit of a Particle System

items.title: Exact weak transport identity for weighted signed vortex particles
items.statement:
Let $x_i:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^2$ be $C^1$ trajectories with fixed real weights $\Gamma_i$, and let $g:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be a common continuous force correction. Suppose
$$\dot x_i(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i(t)-x_j(t))+g(t,x_i(t)),$$
where $K_\varepsilon$ is the mollified kernel in [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]]. For $\omega_N(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$ and every $\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^2)$,
$$\int\varphi d\omega_N(t)-\int\varphi d\omega_N(0) =\int_0^t\int\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot\left(\int K_\varepsilon(x-y)d\omega_N(s)(y)+g(s,x)\right)d\omega_N(s)(x)ds.$$
In particular, the uncorrected regularized particle system satisfies the same weak identity with $g=0$.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; the proof is a finite signed sum.

references.title: J. Liu and X. Xin, Convergence of Vortex Methods for Weak Solutions to the 2-D Euler Equations with Vortex Sheet Data

items.title: One-step Lipschitz bound for classical RK4 on an admitted tube
items.statement:
Let $f:[0,T]\times U\to\mathbb R^m$ be uniformly $L$-Lipschitz in its state variable on a set containing every stage generated by the classical RK4 step of [[def-euler-midpoint-rk4-tableaus]] from any two admitted starting states $u,v$ at the same base time $t$. Assume all these stage evaluations are defined, and let $\Psi_h(t,\cdot)$ be the resulting one-step map for $0<h\le h_0$. Then
$$|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)|\le(1+L_*h)|u-v|,\qquad L_*=Le^{Lh_0}.$$
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used.

references.title: Tobias Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Sections 5.2.3-5.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 18.330, Introduction to Numerical Analysis, Chapter 5

items.title: Tensor composite Simpson error for a two-dimensional force integral
items.statement:
Let $a<b$, $c<d$, let $n_x,n_y\ge2$ be even integers, and set $R=[a,b]\times[c,d]$, $h_x=(b-a)/n_x$, $h_y=(d-c)/n_y$. If $F\in C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ and
$$M_{40}=\max_R|\partial_x^4F|,\qquad M_{04}=\max_R|\partial_y^4F|,$$
then the tensor evaluator of [[alg-tensor-simpson-force-evaluator]] satisfies
$$\left|\int_R F-Q_yQ_xF\right|\le\frac{\sqrt2\,|R|}{180}\bigl(h_x^4M_{40}+h_y^4M_{04}\bigr),\qquad |R|=(b-a)(d-c).$$
Here and in applications of this estimate, $F\in C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ means that each coordinate of $F$ is the restriction to $R$ of a scalar $C^4$ function on an open neighborhood of $R$, in the sense of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. The displayed derivatives are taken coordinatewise from these extensions; their values on $R$ are independent of the extensions, since the extensions agree on the interior and their derivatives are continuous up to the boundary.

On every declared input, if each oracle query returns a value or evaluation-failure, the evaluator terminates with its specified status. For the valid inputs above, with the exact oracle returning $F$ at every grid point, the evaluator terminates and returns a vector after exactly $(n_x+1)(n_y+1)$ oracle queries. This is an exact-arithmetic quadrature bound, not a roundoff estimate.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; all rules are finite exact-arithmetic sums.

references.title: Tobin Driscoll and Richard Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, Section 5.6
MIT OpenCourseWare 18.330, Introduction to Numerical Analysis, Chapter 5

items.title: Fourth-order global error for RK4 on a regularized vortex particle tube
items.statement:
Fix $\varepsilon>0$, finitely many vortex weights, $T>0$, and the regularized finite-particle vector field of [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]], possibly with an added common smooth force correction $g_q(t,X,x_i)$ for spatial force quadrature. Suppose the resulting nonautonomous state field $f(t,X)$ is jointly $C^4$ on an open time-state domain, with derivatives through order four bounded on a common compact convex tube $\mathcal T$ compactly contained in that domain. Assume the exact path, RK4 grid states, and every RK4 stage lie in that tube for $h=T/N\le h_0$, and the common force correction is included in these bounds. Let $C_4$ be a uniform exact-start defect constant, so the local defect is at most $C_4h^5$ as in [[def-one-step-ode-method-local-defect-order-and-stability]]. Let $L_*$ be the stability constant from [[lem-classical-rk4-map-is-lipschitz-on-a-controlled-tube]], so the one-step factor is $1+L_*h$. For exact initialization, the state errors $E_k$ satisfy
$$\max_{0\le k\le N}E_k\le \begin{cases} C_4\dfrac{e^{L_*T}-1}{L_*}h^4,&L_*>0,\\ C_4Th^4,&L_*=0. \end{cases}$$
The tube and stage-admissibility assumptions are conditional; no invariance or global numerical-domain claim is made. The constant $C_4$ may depend on $\varepsilon$, particle count, the quadrature field, and the tube.

For every step $k$, assume all RK4 stages generated from both the exact start $x(t_k)$ and the numerical start $X_k$ lie in $\mathcal T$, and both one-step maps are defined. Let $L$ be a uniform operator-norm bound for $D_Xf$ on $\mathcal T$ and set $L_*=Le^{Lh_0}$, as in the stability lemma. The only admitted start pair used in the stability estimate at step $k$ is $(x(t_k),X_k)$.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used.

references.title: Tobias Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Sections 5.2.3-5.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 18.330, Introduction to Numerical Analysis, Chapter 5

items.title: Mean-field vortex blob error budget with signed particles, force quadrature, and RK4
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $\omega_t$ be a smooth finite signed vorticity density on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^2$ with finite first moment, transported by a sign-preserving characteristic flow $X_t$ satisfying $\omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0$ and $\dot X_t(x)=(K*\omega_t)(X_t(x))$, where $K$ is the singular kernel in [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. Assume $\sup_{t\le T}\|\omega_t\|_\infty\le W$, $\int\sup_{t\le T}|X_t(x)|d|\omega_0|(x)<\infty$, and the flow transports each Jordan part to the corresponding Jordan part. Put $M=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2)$. Let
$$\omega_N^0=\sum_{i=1}^N\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^0}$$
be a finite signed particle measure whose positive and negative Jordan masses respectively equal those of $\omega_0$, with finite first moment, and with consolidated atoms whose positive and negative supports are disjoint; thus $\sum_i|\Gamma_i|=M$. Let $E_0=C_{\pm}(\omega_0,\omega_N^0)<\infty$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$. For every time and force location $(t,x)$, suppose the force integrand $F_{t,x}:R\to\mathbb R^2$ lies in $C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ and its fourth partial derivatives satisfy the uniform bounds $M_{40},M_{04}$. Let the tensor Simpson evaluator use the even panel counts and widths in [[thm-tensor-simpson-force-error]], and define its residual by $r_q(t,x)=Q_yQ_xF_{t,x}-\int_R F_{t,x}$. Thus
$$\eta_q=\frac{\sqrt2|R|}{180}(h_x^4M_{40}+h_y^4M_{04}).$$
Assume this residual is the same correction function for every particle, $\sup_{t,x}|r_q(t,x)|\le\eta_q$, and the corrected regularized particle flow preserves the two Jordan parts. Write $x_i^{\varepsilon,q}$ for the exact solution from $x_i^0$ of
$$\dot x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)-x_j^{\varepsilon,q}(t))+r_q(t,x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)),$$
and set $\omega_N^{\varepsilon,q}(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)}$. Assume the resulting nonautonomous field $f(t,X)$ is jointly $C^4$ on an open time-state domain $D$, with derivatives through order four bounded on a common compact convex tube $\mathcal T\Subset D$ containing all exact paths and RK4 stages. Let $x_i^h(T)$ be the RK4 states from the same initial data for this ODE, and define $\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^h(T)}$. Let $h=T/n\le h_0$ for an integer $n\ge1$ and define $C_{RK}:=C_4(e^{L_*T}-1)/L_*$ if $L_*>0$, and $C_{RK}:=C_4T$ if $L_*=0$, where $C_4,L_*,h_0$ are the constants in [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]]. Then
$$d_{BL}(\omega_T,\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)) \le e^{2L_\varepsilon MT}\left(E_0+MT\left(C_\rho\varepsilon W+\eta_q\right)\right)+MC_{RK}h^4,$$
where $L_\varepsilon$ is a one-variable global Lipschitz constant for $K_\varepsilon$; the induced two-variable constant for $K_\varepsilon(x-y)$ is also $L_\varepsilon$. The terms are initial signed particle approximation, blob regularization, force quadrature, and RK4 time error. The constants may depend on $\varepsilon$, particle count, and the tube; no uniform singular limit as $\varepsilon\to0$ is claimed.

The RK4 tube condition in the Statement includes all numerical grid states and every stage generated at each grid step from both the exact solution start and the numerical start; both one-step maps are defined.
items.axiom_use: The signed branch uses AC for Jordan decompositions and Countable Choice through the polar-coordinate consistency estimate. These are not needed by the separate probability W1 theorem.

title: Interacting particle mean field and vortex blob error — Examples

items.title: Softened Newtonian particles do not specify the physical collision force
items.statement:
For two Newtonian point masses in $\mathbb R^3$ with positive constants absorbed into $c>0$, the unsoftened relative acceleration is $F(r)=-c\,r/|r|^3$ for $r\ne0$, where $|\cdot|$ is Euclidean. A softened model uses
$$F_\varepsilon(r)=-\frac{c r}{(|r|^2+\varepsilon^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \varepsilon>0.$$
The softened field is smooth at a collision, but it defines a different dynamical model.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used.

items.title: A dimension-dependent lower bound for empirical W1 error
items.statement:
Let $M\in\mathbb N$ with $M\ge1$, set $V_M=\{0,1\}^M\subset\mathbb R^M$, and let $\mu_M$ be uniform on its $2^M$ vertices. For any empirical measure $\nu_N=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N\delta_{Y_j}$ obtained from $N$ samples $Y_j\in V_M$, the 1-Wasserstein error has the deterministic lower bound
$$W_1(\mu_M,\nu_N)\ge1-\frac{N}{2^M}.$$
Thus no dimension-free bound $W_1(\mu,\mu_N)\le C N^{-1/2}$ can hold uniformly over all dimensions and all empirical samples.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: A mixed-sign vorticity is not a probability for W1
items.statement: On $\mathbb R^2$, let $\omega=\delta_0-\delta_{(1,0)}$. It is a nonzero finite signed measure of total mass zero and total variation two. The probability $W_1$ in [[def-p-one-wasserstein-one]] cannot be applied to $\omega$.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used.

items.title: A globally Lipschitz alignment model with exact mean trajectory
items.statement: For $a\ge0$ on $\mathbb R^d$, take $K(x,y)=a(y-x)$. For $a>0$, each particle is pulled toward the current mean position; for $a=0$, every particle is stationary. It is globally Lipschitz, and its particle trajectories are explicit.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; the particle calculation is explicit and the cited stability estimate is conditional on its supplied characteristic flows.

references.title: François Golse, Mean-Field Limits in Statistical Dynamics, Lecture 1

items.title: Same-sign smooth vortex density and probability blob error budget
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\omega_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ be nonnegative with mass one, and suppose the smooth Euler flow satisfies $\omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0$, $\dot X_t=(K*\omega_t)(X_t)$, and $\sup_{t\le T}\|\omega_t\|_\infty\le W$, with $\int\sup_{t\le T}|X_t(x)|d\omega_0(x)<\infty$. Approximate it by $N\ge1$ distinct initial positions $x_1^0,\ldots,x_N^0$ with equal weights $1/N$, define $\mu_N^0=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i^0}$, and let $E_0=W_1(\omega_0,\mu_N^0)$.

Let $R=[a,b]\times[c,d]$ with $a<b$ and $c<d$, let $n_x,n_y$ be even integers at least two, and put $h_x=(b-a)/n_x$ and $h_y=(d-c)/n_y$. For every time $t\in[0,T]$ and force location $z\in\mathbb R^2$, let $F_{t,z}\in C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ and assume the uniform bounds
$$\sup_{t\in[0,T],z\in\mathbb R^2}\max_{(x,y)\in R}|\partial_x^4F_{t,z}(x,y)|\le M_{40},\qquad \sup_{t\in[0,T],z\in\mathbb R^2}\max_{(x,y)\in R}|\partial_y^4F_{t,z}(x,y)|\le M_{04}.$$
Define $r_q(t,z)=Q_yQ_xF_{t,z}-\int_RF_{t,z}$ and
$$\eta_q=\frac{\sqrt2|R|}{180}\bigl(h_x^4M_{40}+h_y^4M_{04}\bigr),\qquad |R|=(b-a)(d-c),$$
where $Q_x,Q_y$ are the composite Simpson rules in the two rectangle coordinates. By [[thm-tensor-simpson-force-error]], $|r_q(t,z)|\le\eta_q$ uniformly. Assume this common residual is smooth in $(t,z)$, and let the exact particles solve $\dot x_i=\frac1N\sum_jK_\varepsilon(x_i-x_j)+r_q(t,x_i)$. Assume the resulting nonautonomous field is jointly $C^4$ on an open time-state domain $D$, with derivatives through order four bounded on a common compact convex tube $\mathcal T\Subset D$ containing the exact paths and RK4 stages. For an integer $n\ge1$ with $h=T/n\le h_0$, let $x_i^h(T)$ be their RK4 approximations from the same initial nodes, with all paths and stages in that tube. Define $\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i^h(T)}$. If $C_{RK}$ is the coefficient from [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]] for this $h_0$, then

$$W_1(\omega_T,\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T))\le e^{2L_\varepsilon T}\left(E_0+T(C_\rho\varepsilon W+\eta_q)\right)+C_{RK}h^4.$$

The RK4 tube hypothesis includes all numerical grid states and every stage generated at each grid step from both the exact start and the numerical start, and both one-step maps are defined, as required by [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]].
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used by the cited polar-coordinate kernel estimate; the probability coupling and particle-label arguments use no Axiom of Choice.
